title: Trajectory Sentinel and Go-Live Checklist
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a lightweight operational playbook — the Trajectory Sentinel — for tracking the health and go/no-go signals during a phased product launch. It combines a compact KPI burndown, lane-based rollout sequence, and a Go-Live Checklist with clear owners and rollback triggers. Intended for product-ops owners, SRE, serving-runtime, and launch PMs.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
We will release the feature in four phased lanes across Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private customers. Each lane has a monitors-to-acceptance flow (Signal Tiers 0→3). KPIs are tracked at 15m granularity for the first 72 hours after each ramp step. Primary success criteria: user-facing error rate <0.5% (5xx + bad model outputs), median p95 latency within target, and unit inference cost within 110% of forecast. If any safety or latency signal breaches a Tier-2 threshold we pause the ramp and instrument a canary rollback.

KPI burndown snapshot (single-line records, updated live by analytics):
- KPI: Production API Error Rate (5xx + model decode failures) — target: <0.5% — current: 0.18% — owner: Marcus Green (eng-sre). Trigger Tier-2: >=0.7% sustained 30m.
- KPI: Median p95 latency (end-to-end) — target: <=220ms — current: 210ms — owner: Rafael Torres (serving-runtime). Trigger Tier-2: p95 >350ms 3 consecutive 15m intervals.
- KPI: Token unit cost (inference + infra) — target: forecast * 1.0 — current: 1.04x — owner: Finance liaison (Aisha Patel). Trigger Tier-2: >1.12x for 1 hour.
- KPI: Quality sentinel (regression score on baseline evals) — target: delta >= -0.02 BLEU-equivalent — current: -0.005 — owner: Applied ML (Sana Kapoor). Trigger Tier-3: delta <= -0.03 on critical prompt set.
- KPI: Customer success rate (happy-path completion) for pilot cohort — target: 95% — current: 97% — owner: Solutions Eng (Evan Moore). Trigger Tier-2: <92% in pilot cohort.

Signal tiers (what each level means):
- Tier 0: Informational only. Noncritical metric drift or single-incident anomalies. Document, but no ramp action.
- Tier 1: Advisory. Engineering should investigate within 30 minutes; pre-fail mitigations queued. Consider halting next ramp step.
- Tier 2: Immediate action. Pause traffic increase and prepare rollback. Required triage and postmortem within 24 hours.
- Tier 3: Safety or compliance breach. Immediate rollback to previous stable model/route; notify legal/security and exec pager.

Rollout lanes and percentages (sequence):
1) Internal dogfood (lane-internal) — 0.5% of internal traffic, duration 2h validation. Owner: Product-ops (Lena). Acceptance: no Tier-2 breaches.
2) Beta customers / pilot cohort — 1% external traffic, 6h observe. Owner: Solutions Eng (Evan). Acceptance: Quality sentinel within tolerance + CS sign-off.
3) Gradual customer expansion — 10% over 12h in 3 steps (1%→3%→6%). Owner: Dedicated PM (Priya). Acceptance each step: no Tier-2 breach for 30m post-step.
4) Full production ramp — remaining traffic in 2x capacity steps with autoscale policies. Owner: Product launches (Lena). Acceptance: final KPI stability for 72h.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before first lane):
- [ ] Release notes drafted and verified (owner: PM) — linked: github.com/redwood/docs/pull/741.
- [ ] Canary config created in Console with traffic split and automatic fallback route set (owner: Console team).
- [ ] Autoscaling & GPU reservations validated against expected QPS (owner: infra).
- [ ] Alert playbooks loaded to Ops PagerDuty with runbooks attached (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Security review completed for data ingress in Private deployments (owner: security).
- [ ] Eval prompt set and regression harnesses frozen and uploaded to Optimize (owner: Applied ML).
- [ ] Cost forecast signed off by finance (owner: Aisha Patel).

Go-live immediate actions (first 6 hours of lane):
- 0–15m: sanity smoke — sample 200 calls across models, review for catastrophic decode errors.
- 15–60m: monitor p95, cost, and quality sentinel every 15m. Post any discrepancy to #launch-monitor Slack channel.
- 60–240m: extend sampling to 1k calls/hour, begin customer success outreach for pilot cohort.
- 240–360m: decision point — progress to next lane only if no Tier-2 breaches and PM sign-off.

Rollback & fallback strategy (concrete steps):
1) If Tier-2 trigger fires: Pause traffic increase and divert new sessions to previously pinned model variant or region (Console: Route -> fallback-model). Notify SRE/serving-runtime.
2) If Tier-3: Full rollback — disable new route, re-pin previous model, issue incident bridge. Notify legal/security.
3) If cost overruns exceed threshold: Temporarily enforce token-limit throttles and increase caching/quantization profile for non-critical routes.

Owner matrix (quick contacts):
- Product-ops (overall): Lena Huang — lena@redwood.ai — Slack: @lena
- Eng SRE: Marcus Green — marcus@redwood.ai — PagerDuty: PD-SRE
- Serving runtime: Rafael Torres — rafael@redwood.ai — Slack: #serving-runtime
- Applied ML / Quality: Sana Kapoor — sana@redwood.ai
- Solutions Eng / Pilot CS: Evan Moore — evan@redwood.ai
- Finance liaison: Aisha Patel — aisha@redwood.ai

Post-launch digestion items (24–72h):
- Full incident logs collection and automated sample replay for any anomalous request IDs.
- Regression evaluation run across gold prompt set; produce delta report and quality summary.
- Cost reconciliation vs forecast; propose immediate micro-optimizations (batching tweaks, smaller context limit) if >5% delta.

Open questions & TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Confirm retention policy for intermediate logs for Private deployment customers (privacy/legal input needed).
- Lock the exact canary traffic schedule for Dedicated pools (currently proposed but not finalized).
- Add one synthetic user journey to the SLO dashboard that combines inference latency + end-to-end app time.

Meeting cadence during ramp:
- Live 10m standups every 30m for the first 3 hours after each lane step, then hourly until stable. Attendees: Product-ops, SRE, Serving Runtime, Applied ML, Solutions Eng.

Notes and history:
- v0.1 (2024-03-15): initial draft — Lena.
- v0.2 (2024-03-25): added cost triggers, pilot cohort acceptance criteria — Aisha/ Evan.
- v0.3 (2024-05-02): updated signal tiers and owner matrix; aligned rollback steps with Console team — Rafael.

End of document.
